non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (`authz.opa` and Engine memory rows)
non_blocking.suggestion: With the deterministic estimate (canonical bytes times 4) and a 64 MiB Revision ceiling, one `authz.opa` Policy at its own 16 MiB data cap already reaches the whole ceiling (16 x 4 = 64 MiB), so any module pushes it over and the per-Policy cap cannot be reached in practice. Say so in the row, or propose to Security and identity a per-Policy cap below the Revision ceiling (for example 8 MiB (target)) or per-engine expansion factors.

`ContextEval` only interrupts at comprehension checkpoints when `cel.InterruptCheckFrequency(n)` is set (research section 9.1). Name that option and a value (target). The row cites [Limits], but that section says nothing about the deadline; cite research 9.1 for the deadline half.

'scales linearly from 1 to 32 GOMAXPROCS (target)' has no tolerance, so allocation-driven GC assist makes it fail by construction. State a measurable bound, such as at least 0.8 times linear at 32 (target).

When a context has a deadline, OPA's `Eval` may start a cancellation watcher per call. Add to the Planned (M2) spike a check that this per-call goroutine and channel fit the 100 µs p99 hypothesis, or use one long-lived `topdown.Cancel` path per request.

Say how the per-request principal and resource entities join the Policy's up to 10,000 static entities without a per-request map copy, for example with a layered entity getter over the immutable per-Revision entity map. Add this to the OQ-security-and-identity-18 amendment.

Filter class order puts authz before admission (foundation pack section 8, item 5), so `ratelimit` does not cap the CPU that engines spend. Note that the worst-case fixtures at the caps set the per-request CPU an authenticated caller can force.
Option 4, 'OPA as an external decision service', cites no research URL in the list item. Add the rego.go source used in its cons, or a research URL, so every option is sourced.

'compile once, by digest, across Revisions' and 'data is an immutable per-Revision document' can be read as conflicting. State that the data store is keyed by the same digest, so it is shared, and stays immutable, across Revisions.

Security and identity: add a Cedar entity ancestor-depth cap (target) and a Revision-time transitive-closure precompute for `in`.
